feature: Add rate limiting to authentication endpoints
workflow_rationale: Single-service security hardening task with clear scope - adding @fastify/rate-limit middleware to protect authentication endpoints from brute force attacks. No multi-service coordination needed.

verification.command: cd apps/api && grep -q '@fastify/rate-limit' package.json && echo 'OK' || echo 'FAIL'

subtasks.implementation_notes: Add @fastify/rate-limit to dependencies section. Current Fastify version is 5.0.0, so use compatible rate-limit version (^10.0.0 or later).

verification.command: cd apps/api && test -d node_modules/@fastify/rate-limit && echo 'OK' || echo 'FAIL'

subtasks.implementation_notes: Run 'pnpm install' in the api directory to install the new dependency.

phases.name: Implement Rate Limit Middleware
phases.description: Create and configure rate limiting middleware for authentication endpoints

subtasks.implementation_notes: Create a middleware module that exports rate limit configurations for: (1) Global rate limit (general protection), (2) Auth endpoints rate limit (stricter limits for /api/auth/* routes). Use @fastify/rate-limit with Redis store if available, fallback to in-memory for development. Follow Fastify plugin pattern.

subtasks.description: Register rate limiting middleware in Fastify adapter

verification.command: cd apps/api && grep -q 'rate-limit' src/adapters/fastify.adapter.ts && echo 'OK' || echo 'FAIL'

subtasks.implementation_notes: Import and register rate-limit middleware in createFastifyApp() function. Apply global rate limit first, then register stricter limits for /api/auth/* routes using route-specific configuration. Register after CORS but before controller registration.

phases.name: Security Testing
phases.description: Create comprehensive tests to verify rate limiting works correctly

verification.command: cd apps/api && test -f tests/security/rate-limit.test.ts && echo 'OK' || echo 'FAIL'

subtasks.implementation_notes: Create comprehensive security tests that verify: (1) Rate limit headers are present (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset), (2) Auth endpoints return 429 after exceeding limit, (3) Different endpoints have appropriate rate limits, (4) Rate limits reset after time window. Follow the pattern from owasp.test.ts with server availability check.

subtasks.description: Update existing OWASP security test for rate limiting

verification.command: cd apps/api && grep -q 'X-RateLimit' tests/security/owasp.test.ts && echo 'OK' || echo 'FAIL'

subtasks.implementation_notes: Update the existing 'Rate Limiting' test section (lines 150-158) to actually verify rate limit enforcement rather than just checking graceful handling. Add assertions for 429 status code and rate limit headers.

phases.name: Integration Verification
phases.description: Run all tests and verify rate limiting works end-to-end

subtasks.description: Run security tests and verify rate limiting
subtasks.implementation_notes: Start the API server with 'pnpm dev' in background, then run 'pnpm test:security' to verify all security tests pass, including the new rate limit tests.

subtasks.description: Manual verification of rate limiting on auth endpoints

verification.instructions: With API running, use curl or Postman to: (1) Send multiple requests to POST /api/auth/login, (2) Verify first N requests succeed (200/401), (3) Verify subsequent requests return 429, (4) Verify X-RateLimit-* headers are present, (5) Wait for reset window, (6) Verify requests work again

subtasks.implementation_notes: Perform manual testing to ensure rate limiting works correctly in a real-world scenario. Document the rate limit thresholds and verify they align with security requirements.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: Sequential execution required due to dependencies
